stops.name: Skjálfandi
stops.detail: The peninsula is located in the north of Iceland, bordering the bay Skjálfandi to the west, the Arctic Ocean to the north, and Öxarfjörður to the east.

stops.name: Kópasker
stops.detail: The hypocenter was near the village of Kópasker and the tremors reached a magnitude of 6.2.

days.title: Húsavík and Volcanic Faults
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM start, after checking official access hours

stops.name: Húsavík
stops.detail: The largest town is Húsavík, located on the west side of Skjálfandi, which is the administrative seat of the municipality of Norðurþing.

stops.name: Húsavík-Flatey-Fault
stops.detail: The main actors in this regard are a large tectonic fissure, the so-called Húsavík-Flatey-Fault, also known as Húsavík-Transform-Fault, and the Þeistareykir volcanic system.

stops.name: Þeistareykjabunga
stops.detail: The tectonic fissure cuts through the urban area of Húsavík, where it is clearly visible and forms a natural harbor, and then runs east into the mountains to end at the central volcano Þeistareykjabunga.
